about.title: Vista Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Vista sits where SR-78 threads through northern San Diego County, and that highway, along with E Vista Way, S Melrose Drive, and Vista Village Drive, accounts for the largest share of the city's reported collisions. In 2025, public records show 212 injury collisions in Vista, with 311 people hurt and 4 lives lost. Reports cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters heading home mix with weekend traffic. If you were one of those 311 people, the days after a crash can feel like paperwork stacked on top of pain. Adjusters call quickly. Repair estimates arrive. Medical bills follow. LawProactive exists to simplify one part of that: we connect you, at no cost, with an independent personal injury attorney who handles Vista car accident claims. You talk with them directly about what happened on Melrose or the 78, and they explain how California's pure comparative fault rule and two-year filing deadline apply to your situation. We are not a law firm, and there is no fee to be matched.

whyChoose.title: What a Vista Car Accident Attorney Can Do for You

items.title: Keep the two-year clock from running out
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit, but a claim involving a public agency can require notice in as little as six months. An attorney tracks those dates so a missed deadline never decides your case.

items.title: Push back when fault gets shared
items.desc: Under pure comparative fault, you can still recover even if you were partly to blame, with your award reduced by your percentage. Insurers often try to inflate that percentage, and your attorney works to keep the split honest.

items.title: Protect your evidence and your words
items.desc: Photos from the scene, dashcam footage, and witness names fade fast, and a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer can be used against you. Your attorney preserves what helps and handles the adjuster so you don't have to.

items.question: My crash happened on SR-78 in Vista. Does it matter that it's a state highway?
items.answer: It can. SR-78 is maintained by Caltrans, so if a road condition or a government vehicle played a role, part of your claim may involve a public entity, and California requires a government claim within six months rather than the usual two years. Most SR-78 collisions are simply between private drivers, but an attorney can sort out which rules apply to yours quickly.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company keeps calling. Should I give them a statement?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it is usually wise not to before speaking with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shift fault onto you under California's comparative fault rule. Let your own insurer know about the crash as your policy requires, and let an attorney handle the rest.

items.question: How much does it cost to be connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, and we are not a law firm. The independent attorneys in our network handle car accident cases on contingency, which means they are paid a percentage of any recovery and you owe no attorney fee if there is none.
